content.value_statement: Concurrent Go code can leak goroutines, race on data, or ignore cancellation. This skill guides implementation with proven patterns, examples, and verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains goroutines, channels, select, sync.Mutex, sync.WaitGroup, and context.Context.
Provides worker pool patterns with context-aware jobs and result channels.
Shows fan-out and fan-in pipelines with cancellation-aware stages.
Demonstrates bounded concurrency with semaphore-based limits.
Covers graceful shutdown, errgroup cancellation, sync.Map, and sharded maps.
Lists race detector commands and concurrency best practices.
limitations: It provides instructional examples and does not run or test code automatically.
Examples may need adaptation for application-specific error handling and resource limits.
It focuses on Go concurrency, not full application architecture or deployment.
It does not replace race tests, load tests, or production observability.

use_cases.title: Implement Worker Pools
use_cases.description: Design bounded worker pools that process jobs, return results, and stop when context is canceled.

use_cases.title: Add Graceful Shutdown
use_cases.description: Plan service shutdown flows that stop goroutines, wait for cleanup, and respect timeouts.

use_cases.title: Review Concurrency Safety
use_cases.description: Check pull requests for goroutine leaks, unsafe shared state, channel misuse, and missing race tests.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how a Go worker pool works. Include when to use it, how context cancellation fits, and common mistakes to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Concurrency Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a new feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to process many independent jobs in Go with bounded parallelism. Recommend a concurrency pattern and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Race or Leak
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go concurrency design for goroutine leaks, data races, blocked sends, and missing cancellation paths. Provide prioritized fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Service Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Go service workflow for shutdown safety, errgroup usage, backpressure, resource limits, and race detector coverage.

output_examples.input: I need to process thousands of jobs without exhausting memory or goroutines.
output: Recommend a bounded worker pool with a fixed worker count and buffered job input.
Use context cancellation so workers exit when the request or service stops.
Return structured results and errors through a result channel.
Verify behavior with race detection and load tests.

output_examples.input: My Go service hangs during shutdown after receiving a termination signal.
output: Trace every started goroutine and confirm each has a cancellation or close path.
Use a shutdown timeout so cleanup cannot block forever.
Wait for worker completion with a synchronization primitive.
Avoid using sleep as the shutdown coordination mechanism.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds shared maps across goroutines.
output: Check whether the workload is read-heavy or write-heavy before choosing sync.Map.
Use locks or sharding when normal maps are shared across goroutines.
Confirm tests run with the Go race detector.
Document ownership rules for shared state.

best_practices: Pass context through goroutines and check cancellation paths.
Use channels for communication, and protect shared state when memory must be shared.
Run race detection and load tests after changing concurrency logic.
anti_patterns: Starting goroutines without a clear stop condition.
Closing channels from receivers or from multiple senders.
Using time.Sleep as a synchronization mechanism.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design and review concurrent Go code using goroutines, channels, context, worker pools, pipelines, and synchronization primitives.

faq.question: Can it find data races automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend race detection steps, but you must run Go tooling in your own project.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready code for every service?
faq.answer: No. The examples are patterns that need adaptation for your service limits, errors, dependencies, and observability.

faq.question: When should I use channels instead of mutexes?
faq.answer: Use channels for coordination and ownership transfer. Use mutexes when shared state is simpler and ownership is clear.

faq.question: Does it cover graceful shutdown?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes context cancellation, signal handling, wait groups, cleanup timeouts, and worker lifecycle guidance.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides structured guidance that these AI coding tools can use when helping with Go concurrency tasks.
